questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Diagnoses disk pressure across diverse filesystems in real deployments. Requires precise parsing of df outputs, handling spaces, and edge cases like pseudo filesystems. A pragmatic check supports reliability in production.

## Key Concepts
- df usage and -P portability
- inode vs block usage metrics
- robust parsing with awk/shell while handling spaces
- filtering pseudo filesystems

## Code Example
```bash
# robust per-mount health check (blocks and inodes)
df -P | awk 'NR>1{mount=$NF; blocks[switch(mount)]=substr($5,1,length($5)-1); mounts[mount]=1} END{for (m in blocks) print m":"" blocks="blocks[m]"%""," inodes="inodes[m]"%"" - ok"}'
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this to exclude network filesystems reliably across distros?
- How would you alert if a mount becomes critical only during peak load windows?

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses ability to inspect processes and time-based conditions from /proc with POSIX tools, focusing on runtime security and privilege boundaries.

## Key Concepts
- /proc/[pid]/status Uid fields (real vs. effective)
- /proc/[pid]/stat starttime and clock ticks
- /proc/uptime and getconf CLK_TCK for time calculations
- Mapping UID to usernames via getent

## Code Example
```bash
#!/bin/sh
uptime=$(cat /proc/uptime | awk '{print $1}')
clk=$(getconf CLK_TCK)
for p in /proc/[0-9]*; do
  [ -r "$p/status" ] || continue
  ruid=$(awk '/^Uid:/ {print $2}' "$p/status" 2>/dev/null)
  euid=$(awk '/^Uid:/ {print $3}' "$p/status" 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$ruid" ] || continue
  st=$(awk '{print $22}' "$p/stat" 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$st" ] || continue
  age=$(( (uptime - (st/clk)) ))
  [ "$euid" != "$ruid" ] && [ "$age" -le 300 ] && cmd=$(tr '\0' ' ' < "$p/cmdline" 2>/dev/null)
  user=$(getent passwd "$ruid" | cut -d: -f1)
  printf "%s %s %s %s %s\n" "${p##*/}" "$user" "$cmd" "$euid" "$ruid"
done
```
